---
title: "The evidence platform"
---

The [Bigger Picture evidence platform](https://motivation-and-behaviour.github.io/bigger-picture-platform/) is the public website that presents the project's research as short, plain-language **evidence summaries** for teachers.
This section is for research assistants who write and update those summaries.

You write summaries in **Airtable**.
You never need to touch code, Markdown files or the platform's GitHub repository, apart from pressing a button to publish.

## What a summary is

Each summary covers **one type of screen use**, called an *exposure* (for example "Social media" or "Educational TV & video"), and brings together all the research we have on it.
On the website, a summary has these parts:

| Part | What it shows |
|------|---------------|
| Overall rating | One impact rating and one confidence rating for the exposure as a whole. This is the headline on the overview card and at the top of the page. |
| What is it? | A short definition of the exposure. |
| Key findings | The evidence grouped by **outcome domain** (e.g. Mental health). Each specific outcome in a domain has its own impact and evidence-quality rating. |
| How effects differ | How the effect varies with age, sex, dose and so on. |
| What can I do? | Practical strategies for teachers, each linked back to the evidence. |
| About the evidence | How many meta-analyses, studies and participants the summary draws on, and which sources. |
| References | Full citations, numbered. |

Read a published summary, such as [Social media](https://motivation-and-behaviour.github.io/bigger-picture-platform/evidence/social-media/), before you write your first one.

## The two ratings

Every finding gets two ratings:

- **Impact**, from −3 (strong harmful relationship) through 0 (no clear relationship) to +3 (strong beneficial relationship).
- **Evidence quality**, from 1 (very low confidence) to 5 (very high confidence), or 0 when there isn't enough evidence to rate.

How to choose them is set out in [Rating the evidence](rating-the-evidence.qmd).
The website explains the scales to its readers on its [How we rate](https://motivation-and-behaviour.github.io/bigger-picture-platform/how-we-rate/) page.

## How your work reaches the website

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A[You edit in Airtable] --> B[Publish button<br/>or nightly run]
  B --> C{The sync checks<br/>each summary}
  C -- valid --> D[Website updated]
  C -- problem --> E[Sync status:<br/>Needs fixing]
```

- **Airtable is the only place to edit.** The website's files are generated from it, so anything changed elsewhere is overwritten.
- **The Status field controls what is published.**
  - *Draft* summaries never leave Airtable.
  - *Preliminary* summaries are published with a "Preliminary summary" banner, which tells readers the summary hasn't yet been checked by the review team.
  - *Reviewed* summaries are published without the banner.
- **A problem in one summary never blocks the others.** If a published summary develops a problem, its last good version stays live until you fix it.
- **The sync reports back.** After each run, every summary's *Sync status* and *Sync message* fields in Airtable say whether it was published and, if not, exactly what to fix.

## What you need access to

- **Airtable**: an invitation to edit the *Bigger Picture summaries* base. Editor places are limited, so ask the platform maintainer.
- **GitHub** (optional): to publish straight away with the Publish button, you need a GitHub account with write access to the [`bigger-picture-platform`](https://github.com/Motivation-and-Behaviour/bigger-picture-platform) repository, which is private: ask the platform maintainer. Without it, your work still publishes automatically overnight.
- **The umbrella review data**: the Bigger Picture umbrella review's complete effects data ([Supplementary File 6](https://github.com/Motivation-and-Behaviour/screen_umbrella/tree/main/supplementary_files) in the `screen_umbrella` repository) has child- and adolescent-specific estimates for most of the reviews you will use.
